1. The first <BIBL> element was never closed properly around the "Prideaux" entry — the mis-tagged <PRIZE>Cattenburg</PRIZE> was actually an author name beginning the next bibliographic entry. I closed the first <BIBL> after the volume/price information and moved "Cattenburg" into a new <BIBL> as <AUTHOR>.
2. Removed the erroneous <PRIZE> tag (Cattenburg is a personal name, not a price) and replaced it with <AUTHOR>.
3. The second <BIBL> ("Sapientia Mos. ...") was not closed before a nested <BIBL> ("Bibl. ... 8r. 70.") was opened; nested BIBL elements are not valid here, so I closed the "Sapientia Mos." entry after its <FORMAT>4.</FORMAT> and made the following entry a sibling <BIBL>.
4. Escaped the raw ampersand in "de Vita & Scriptis Mosis" as "&" so the XML is well-formed.
5. In the "Bibl. Hebr." entry the word "von" preceded <AUTHOR>punctata Leusdenii</AUTHOR>; kept the text but normalised so that the title element carries "Bibl. Hebr. punctata" and the author is "Leusdenii", which reflects the actual bibliographic reference (Biblia Hebraica punctata by Johannes Leusden).
6. Normalised the stray "√†" character (a corrupted currency/price marker) by wrapping the price information of the first entry in a <PRIZE> element.
All other mojibake characters were left untouched, as they belong to the source transcription and are not XML errors.
